chapter: Rhythm and blues, the Howard Theatre and later years
title: Jazz dying in 1954 as rock and roll arrives
summary: Harry Curtis led a band of a few gigs around 1954, when jazz work was disappearing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Then what did you do in '54?
Harry Curtis, he got a band.
He was in that band of yours at one time.

Yeah, he was in there with John. He got a band himself around '54. We just gigged. That was about three gigs. Doin' pretty good. The music was dying then. That's when it was goin' down, round about '54. Rock-and-Roll was comin' in like Faust. Rock-and-Roll and Rhythm-and-Blues. People wasn't carin' about no Jazz too much then.
